dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Rosa. How can I help you?

Hi Rosa, hi. Oh, good, a real person. So I'm sitting in my car in the parking lot at the pharmacy, because I was supposed to pick up a prescription at eleven and of course the line was out the door, so I figured I'd make this call while I wait. Is that okay? Am I breaking up?
You're coming through fine. Go ahead.

Okay good. Because my cell is a mess lately. Honestly I'm shopping for a better phone plan, I keep dropping calls, and I'm paying way too much for it. But that's not why I'm calling. Well, kind of. Anyway. I'm Beatriz Pagan. I rent at 325 Van Zandt Avenue, up in the North End.
Okay, Ms. Pagan. Three twenty-five Van Zandt. What's going on?

So it's two things and they're tied together. Last weekend, that snow turning to rain storm, Sunday into Monday, the wind took down a whole section of the fence between my yard and the neighbor's. Just flat. Boards everywhere. And I want to know who pays for that. Is it me, is it the neighbor, is it the city? Because I'm a renter, so I don't even know if it's mine.
Okay. Sorry about the fence. Who owns the fence usually comes down to the property line and who put it up. Is it on your side, the neighbor's side, or right on the line?

That's the thing, nobody knows! It's right on the line, more or less. My landlord says it's the neighbor's. The neighbor says it's my landlord's. And meanwhile the neighbor, this is the part that gets me, he has been running some kind of generator, or a compressor, I don't know what, in his back shed at night. Again. It's been going for weeks.
Okay, so you also have a noise issue with him.

Yes. Weeks. Last night it was going until, I don't know, almost one in the morning. And it hums, it's this low rattling thing, and I can feel it in my bedroom wall. I've asked him nicely twice. He just waves at me. Waves! Like that fixes it.

I hear you. So let me separate these. On the fence, the city doesn't decide who pays between neighbors. That's between the owners, the property line, and sometimes insurance. I can't tell you whose it is.
Right, but the storm did it. Doesn't the city do anything when a storm wrecks stuff? I mean it's not like anybody did it on purpose.

No, the city doesn't pay to repair private fences after a storm. If it's insured, the owner's homeowner's policy might cover it, so your landlord or the neighbor would want to check that. If you have renter's insurance, it generally covers your belongings, not the fence itself.
Ugh. So it's just nobody's problem until somebody decides it is.
Pretty much, unless there's a safety issue. Are the boards in the street or on a sidewalk, anything blocking people?
No, no, it's all in the yards. But it's wide open now, so his dog comes right into my yard. And that's one more thing I'm tired of.
Okay. I'd suggest your landlord write to the neighbor, or the two of them sort it out, and take photos of the fence now before anybody cleans it up. That helps with insurance.
I took about ten photos Monday morning. I was out there in my slippers in the slush. Soaked. Fine. So that I did right.
Good. Now the noise. Does the machine run at night, you said, every night?

Most nights. Starting around nine, ten. I've got it written down on the back of an envelope, honestly. Last night till almost one. Sunday night it was off because of the storm, probably the power. Monday it was back.

Okay, good. Keep that log with dates and times. For ongoing noise at night, you can file a complaint, and since it's at night and it's repeated, I'd also say call the police non-emergency line when it's actually happening, because they can come and hear it in real time. I can take your complaint here and send it to the right office as well.
I don't love calling the police on a neighbor. It feels harsh. But I'm not sleeping, so, I guess.
It's not an emergency call, it's the regular line, and it's what it's for. A written record helps too. So let me get your details. Your name again, spelled for me?
Beatriz, B-E-A-T-R-I-Z. Pagan, P-A-G-A-N.
Thank you. And the address is three twenty-five Van Zandt Avenue. And the neighbor, which side?
The one to the left if you're facing the house from the street. I don't know his last name. I only know the dog's name, which is sad.
That's fine, the address will do. Do you know the number?

I think it's three twenty-seven. Or three twenty-three. Hold on, I'm going to say three twenty-seven, but don't hold me to it. [pause] Sorry, the pharmacy guy is waving at me, no, he's not, never mind.
No problem. I'll note left side, possibly three twenty-seven, and we can confirm. What's a good callback number?
401-555-0175. And if it drops, just call back, my phone does that.
Got it, 401-555-0175. I'll write it up as a repeated nighttime noise complaint from a machine in a rear shed, and someone will follow up. I can't promise exactly when, but it'll go in today.
Okay. And honestly, that's what I wanted, because I'm so tired of this. The fence, fine, I'll push my landlord. But the humming, that's been going on and on, and nobody's done anything.
I understand. You've been patient. Keep logging it, and if it's going while you're on the phone with the police, tell them you've already filed with us.
Okay, will do. Thank you, Rosa. Sorry I rambled about my phone plan.
No worries at all. Hope the line moves along. Take care, Ms. Pagan.
You too. Bye.
